clue.text: Contemptible centre of operations

definitions.meaning: first meaning: low, mean, morally despicable
second meaning: a headquarters or home station

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests a despised headquarters; the two parts are separate meanings, an adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for ignoble behaviour and a noun for a military or business headquarters.

clue.text: Mostly support quantity of gold for gambling game

indicators.note: most of the word but not all, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to back is to support
a carat measures the purity of gold

explanation.surface: Someone props up a large stake of gold to play a casino game.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a card game played in casinos for stakes, a classic form of gambling.

clue.text: A lot of icy weather beginning to penetrate nap

indicators.note: a lot of the word, but not all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: sleet is half-frozen rain

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: only its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A spell of freezing weather interrupts someone's afternoon doze.
explanation.definitionFit: A nap is a short rest, and to sleep is the verb, also usable as a noun for a short period of slumber.

clue.text: Sword: I'm the very thing to cut lasting mark

indicators.note: the inner pieces slice into the outer word, ending up inside it

parts.note: a scar is a permanent mark on the skin
taken as written
'it' is the very thing, the ideal, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: A sword boasts of being the perfect blade to leave a permanent scar.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved single-edged sword of Middle Eastern origin.

clue.text: One interrogating angry ex, a pitman?

parts.note: cross means annoyed
taken as written
taken as written
a pitman works in a coal pit

explanation.surface: Someone questions a furious former partner who happens to be a coal miner.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-examiner questions a witness called by the other side in a trial.

clue.text: Important judge participating in climbing range

indicators.note: the letter takes part by sitting inside the other word
in a down clue, climbing means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: to range is to roam, wander widely

explanation.surface: A senior judge takes part in an expedition up a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Major means significant or of great consequence, the opposite of minor.

clue.text: A lot of alarm with time running short over getting drums

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second
the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a lot of the word but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: panic is sudden alarm

explanation.surface: A musician, panicking with time running out, gets hold of the drums.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums, the large tuned percussion of an orchestra.

clue.text: Demonstration, not heading for top of building

indicators.note: without its heading, the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a proof demonstrates that something is true

explanation.surface: A protest is held, but not at the top of the building.
explanation.walkthrough: Demonstration suggests a protest march; here it means a proof.
explanation.definitionFit: The roof is the covering structure at the very top of a building.

clue.text: Enthusiast embracing King as chum

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other letter within it

parts.note: a fiend is a devotee, as in 'a fitness fiend'

explanation.surface: A royal fan hugs the King as if he were a mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Chum is an informal word for a close pal or companion.

clue.text: Happiness initially is only for so long

parts.note: cheer is gladness or good spirits

indicators.note: takes the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A gloomy reflection that happiness lasts only for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For so long' is a disguised 'so long', a farewell, not a length of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is a British informal goodbye, just as 'so long' is a casual farewell.

clue.text: Large crossword needed for journey in this?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: The Times prints an extra-big crossword called a ...
second meaning: the aircraft you travel in

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a big puzzle to pass time on a long trip; the second meaning is the jumbo jet itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo names both the oversized holiday crossword and the Boeing 747 airliner.

clue.text: Quantity of statistical data, initially sufficient

indicators.note: the word loses its initial letter

parts.note: a sample is a portion of data collected for statistical analysis

explanation.surface: A statistician judges that the first batch of data will be enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, more than enough for the need.

clue.text: Setback for the French, about to broadcast several programmes

indicators.note: set back means put in reverse, so the whole is read backwards
the French article goes round the other word

parts.note: les is the French plural 'the'
to air a show is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: French television suffers a setback when it comes to broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial is a story told across a sequence of episodes or instalments.

clue.text: Vision certainly possessed by rowing squad

indicators.note: held inside the other word

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
yes, certainly

explanation.surface: A rowing crew definitely has good vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, the sense of sight.

clue.text: Handy skill imitated by Rex, somehow

indicators.note: in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the thirteen letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Rex copies someone else's practical knack, one way or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' is a pun: the skill is using either hand equally well.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambidexterity is the ability to use both hands with equal ease, a skill literally of the hands.

clue.text: Wedding participants carrying grand crosses

indicators.note: the outer word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: brides are central participants in a wedding
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Brides carry something grand as they cross the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridge a river or gap is to span it, so bridges is a verb meaning spans.

clue.text: Specialist to strain to restrict power

indicators.note: to restrict is to confine, so the outer word encloses the letter

parts.note: to exert oneself is to strain

explanation.surface: An engineer strains to limit the electrical power.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is a person with specialised knowledge in a field.

clue.text: Rest arrive briefly for TV programme

parts.note: to sit is to rest

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: Relaxing in front of the TV for a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom is a situation comedy, a television genre.

clue.text: Expression of surprise over US soldier's dog

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the sight of an American soldier's dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed, famously kept by the late Queen.

clue.text: Very good soup I cooked

indicators.note: cooking reworks ingredients, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A cook boasts of the excellent soup they made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very good' looks like praise of the soup; it means morally good, devout.
explanation.definitionFit: Pious describes a devout, virtuous person, very good in a religious sense.

clue.text: Numbers upset after eating one vegetable

indicators.note: the outer letters take the other in
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so reversed

parts.note: two numbers, each abbreviated NO

explanation.surface: Diners are upset by the figures after eating a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is a bulb vegetable used widely in cooking.

clue.text: Part of speech never bettered, but only part

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, the answer sits inside them

parts.note: the answer runs across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A grammar claim that some element of language is unsurpassed, though only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb is a word class naming actions or states, one of the parts of speech.

clue.text: Enthusiastic period enshrined by former monarch

indicators.note: held inside, as in a shrine

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A historian keen on an era immortalised by a past queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen, impatient to do something.

clue.text: Hurry back to celebrate caring vocation

indicators.note: the word is read backwards

parts.note: to run is to hurry
to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: Rushing home to celebrate a career in looking after people.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursing is the profession of caring for the sick.

clue.text: Foremost record of year disposing of duke's animal book

parts.note: best means top, foremost

indicators.note: the letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: a diary records the days of a year
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A duke throws out a leading yearly journal in favour of a book about animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestiary is a medieval collection of descriptions of real and mythical beasts.

clue.text: One out of condition is losing heart

indicators.note: the heart of the word, its middle letter, is removed

parts.note: unfit means not in good shape

explanation.surface: Someone out of shape loses courage.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, the number one.
